meta.purpose: Golden PR-review scenarios for evaluating agents that review and raise pull requests on OpenTelemetry code. Each scenario describes a code change and the findings/reviewers/affected components a correct, knowledge-grounded review must surface. The knowledge graph is the source of truth for ownership, stability, supported signals, dependents and the responsible SIG.
meta.how_to_use: (1) Retrieval grounding: src/evaluate.py runs `retrieval_query` against the graph and scores whether the expected reviewers, affected dependents and grounding facts are surfaced. (2) Agent scoring: call evaluate.score_review(agent_findings, scenario) with an external review agent's findings (each tagged with a `key`) to get precision/recall against `expected_findings`.

scenarios.title: Breaking config rename in the stable OTLP receiver
scenarios.pr_description: Rename the `grpc` config block to `grpc_settings` in the OTLP receiver to make the schema more consistent.
scenarios.retrieval_query: OTLP receiver stability in the opentelemetry-collector repository and which SIG owns it and what depends on it

expected_findings.finding: otlpreceiver is a STABLE component; renaming a config field is a breaking change that violates stability guarantees and must be avoided or staged with deprecation + alias.
opentelemetry-collector-contrib depends on the core collector; a breaking config change can ripple into contrib distributions and user configs.
A changelog entry (.chloggen) describing the breaking change is required.

scenarios.title: New contrib exporter without metadata.yaml or code owners
scenarios.pr_description: Add a new acmeexporter that ships traces to the ACME backend.
scenarios.retrieval_query: requirements for adding a new exporter to opentelemetry-collector-contrib and which SIG owns it

expected_findings.finding: A new contrib component must include a metadata.yaml declaring its class, stability and supported signals.
Contrib components require at least one active code owner in metadata.yaml; a new component cannot merge without a sponsoring code owner.
A README documenting configuration and a changelog entry are required for new components.

scenarios.title: Add a field to the OTLP protobuf definitions
scenarios.pr_description: Add an optional `span_flags` field to the Span message in the trace proto.
scenarios.retrieval_query: what depends on opentelemetry-proto and which SIG owns OTLP and the OpenTelemetry protocol

expected_findings.finding: OTLP is a stable wire protocol; proto changes must be backward/forward compatible (additive, optional fields only) and follow the OTLP versioning rules.
Every language SDK depends on opentelemetry-proto; a proto change requires coordinated rollout across the SDK repositories.
Protocol/spec changes are governed by the Specification SIG and may require spec-sponsor approval or an OTEP.

scenarios.title: Rename an HTTP semantic-convention attribute
scenarios.pr_description: Rename http.request.method back to http.method across the HTTP conventions.
scenarios.retrieval_query: where are the http semantic conventions defined and which SIG owns semantic conventions

expected_findings.finding: Changing a semantic-convention attribute requires a schema version bump and a schema transformation so consumers can migrate.
HTTP conventions are consumed by instrumentation across every language; a rename is broadly breaking and needs the stability/deprecation process.
The Semantic Conventions SIG owns this area and must approve attribute changes.

scenarios.title: Add a new optional config option to the Kafka exporter
scenarios.pr_description: Add an optional `compression` setting (default none) to the Kafka exporter.
scenarios.retrieval_query: kafka exporter stability, supported signals and who maintains it

expected_findings.finding: kafkaexporter is beta; an optional, backward-compatible config addition with a sensible default is acceptable.
The change must be approved by the Kafka exporter's active code owners (axw, MovieStoreGuy, paulojmdias, pavolloffay).
Update the component README and add a changelog entry for the new option.

scenarios.title: Change the Tracer API surface in the specification
scenarios.pr_description: Add a new required parameter to Tracer.startSpan in the API specification.
scenarios.retrieval_query: which specification defines the Tracer and Span and which repositories implement the API specification and who owns the specification

expected_findings.finding: The Tracer/Span API is defined by the API Specification and is stable; a new required parameter is a breaking API change requiring strong justification and likely an OTEP.
Every language SDK implements the API specification, so this change forces coordinated updates across all SDK repositories.
Specification changes are owned by the Specification SIG and require spec-sponsor / Technical Committee review.
